question: Apple's 2025 Environmental Progress Report charts its transition to certified recycled materials by product line (Apple Watch, Desktop, Laptop, iPad, iPhone) for 2017, 2019, 2021 and 2024. According to that chart: (a) in 2024, for which materials do all five product lines show certified recycled content in all products launched that year? (b) In 2024, which product lines show that status for lithium, and which for cobalt (and what does the chart show for the other lines' cobalt)? (c) Which material and product line is the earliest case of 'all products launched' in the chart, and in which year? (d) What does the chart show for tungsten in Desktop, Laptop and iPad?

facets.text: 2024, all five lines with certified recycled content in all products launched: copper, gold, rare earth elements, aluminum, tin and plastic (six materials).

evidence.what: dot chart 'Our transition to certified recycled materials by product line', 2024 block

facets.text: 2024 lithium: iPhone only. 2024 cobalt: Apple Watch and iPhone (all products); Laptop shows 'some products'; Desktop and iPad show none.

evidence.what: dot chart, 2024 block, lithium and cobalt rows

facets.text: The earliest 'all products launched' mark is plastic for Desktop in 2017 (in 2017 Laptop, iPad and iPhone show 'some products' for plastic and every other cell is empty).

(Grading: optional - the footnote to 'Tungsten*' defines 'not applicable', so this can be inferred from the text) Tungsten for Desktop, Laptop and iPad is shown as a dash - recycled content 'not applicable' (found only in trace amounts dispersed across modules) - in 2021 and 2024; in 2017 and 2019 these cells are white.

evidence.what: dot chart, tungsten row and legend

reference_answer: (a) In 2024 copper, gold, rare earth elements, aluminum, tin and plastic are filled (all products launched) for all five lines. (b) Lithium: only iPhone. Cobalt: Apple Watch and iPhone filled, Laptop half-tone (some products), Desktop and iPad empty. (c) Plastic in Desktop products, 2017 - the only filled cell that year. (d) A dash: recycled content is not applicable for tungsten in those lines (2021 and 2024; in 2017 and 2019 the cells are white).
notes: PDF p.17 (printed 17). Legend: dark = all products launched in the calendar year include certified recycled content; grey = some; white = none; dash = not applicable. Docling keeps the row and column labels as an empty table, so the cell states exist only in the image. Near misses: steel in 2024 is dark for Apple Watch, Laptop and iPhone but grey for Desktop and white for iPad; zinc is grey for Desktop only; the text above the chart names 100 percent recycled cobalt in the iPhone 16 battery, which matches but does not answer (b).

question: In NIST SP 800-37 Rev. 2, Figure G-1 (conceptual view of a complex system) shows a system made of subsystems. How many subsystems and system elements are drawn? Which subsystems are directly connected to each other, which subsystem connects to the 'Other System', and which subsystems connect to the two enabling systems? Where is the Other System drawn relative to the authorization boundary and the environment of operation?

facets.text: (Grading: optional - the counts can also be read from the text layer) Three subsystems, each with three system elements (nine in total).
Subsystem 1 is connected to Subsystem 2, and Subsystem 2 to Subsystem 3; Subsystems 1 and 3 are not directly connected.

evidence.what: Figure G-1 dashed two-way arrows between subsystems

facets.text: Subsystem 2 connects to the Other System; the left enabling system connects to Subsystem 1 and the right enabling system to Subsystem 3.

(Grading: optional - Chapter 2 says other systems are outside the authorization boundary and in the operational environment) The Other System sits outside the system's authorization boundary but inside the environment of operation (the enabling systems sit at the outer edge of the environment of operation).

reference_answer: Three subsystems with three system elements each. Subsystem 1 links to Subsystem 2 and Subsystem 2 to Subsystem 3 (no direct 1-3 link). Subsystem 2 links to the Other System, Subsystem 1 to the left enabling system and Subsystem 3 to the right one. The Other System is inside the environment of operation but outside the authorization boundary; all links are dashed two-way arrows.
notes: PDF p.176 (printed 157). The text only says Figure G-1 illustrates a complex system; Docling keeps the labels (SUBSYSTEM 1-3, System Element, Enabling System, Other System) but not the arrows.

question: The Business section of Harbin Yuyantang's prospectus includes a manufacturing flowchart for its TCM dosage forms. After 'TCM decocting pieces' and 'Dispensing & blending', into which two processing lines does the flow split? From which line does each dosage form - paste, granules, pills and powder - branch, and what steps follow each before packaging? What happens after packaging?

facets.text: Two lines: an extraction line (soaking -> decoction -> filtration -> concentration) and a drying -> grinding line.
(Grading: optional - the text says paste is made from concentrated extracts) Paste comes off the extraction line, then paste formation.

(Grading: optional - the text's technique descriptions give the granule steps) Granules come off the extraction line (the arrow leaves its frame under concentration), then granulation -> drying -> granule sizing.
Pills come off the drying-grinding line (the arrow leaves under drying), then pill sizing -> sieving.
Powder comes off the drying-grinding line (under grinding), then mixing.

(Grading: optional - the label order gives it) All four branches then enter the final group: packaging -> inspection & test -> release. (The arrows from sieving and mixing meet that group's frame above inspection & test and release; reading them as entering the packaging group is intended, and noting their literal end points is not penalized.)

reference_answer: After dispensing and blending the flow splits into an extraction line (soaking, decoction, filtration, concentration) and a drying-grinding line. Paste and granules come off the extraction line: paste goes through paste formation, granules through granulation, drying and granule sizing. Pills and powder come off the drying-grinding line: pills (drawn under drying) go through pill sizing and sieving, powder (under grinding) through mixing. All four enter the final group of packaging, then inspection & test, then release.
notes: PDF p.163 (printed 155). Docling keeps the box labels in reading order but not the arrows ('Grinding' is missing from the extracted text). The text below describes each technique but not which dosage form follows which path; it says paste is made from concentrated extracts (so f2 is optional; the technique descriptions and the label order also give the granule steps and the final group, so f3 and f6 are optional), and its 'granule sizing & pill sizing: dried extract powder ...' suggests pills come from the extraction line, which the chart does not show. Lines are graded, not the step under which an arrow leaves a line's frame (the paste arrow leaves under decoction).
